html:
Erebuni is a fortress on a hill at the southern edge of Yerevan, founded in 782 BCE by King Argishti I of Urartu, as a cuneiform inscription found on the site records.

Urartu was the Iron Age kingdom of the Armenian highlands and a rival of Assyria. Erebuni guarded its northern lands and held a palace, temples and storerooms for grain and wine. The name Erebuni is thought to have become Yerevan, which celebrated its 2,750th anniversary in 2018, making it one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities. After Urartu fell in the 500s BCE, the Armenians, speaking an Indo-European language, emerged as the main people of the region under Persian rule.
